qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Local sheet and box converting plants create regional freight switching friction (corrugated boxes have low value-to-bulk, limiting economic shipping to 150-200 miles). However, containerboard and linerboard are standardized industrial commodities with benchmark index pricing (RISI). IP cannot earn returns above its cost of capital across the cycle: 10-year median ROIC is ~6.5%, far below the 12% threshold. Margins are compressed whenever industry capacity expands or input costs (energy, virgin fiber, OCC) rise, as price increases lag and face intense buyer resistance.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 6.5% vs. 12% threshold, REJECT). Standardized commodity containerboard producer lacking structural pricing power. 10-year median ROIC of 6.5% reflects cyclical price-taking behavior and heavy capital intensity, exacerbated by post-DS Smith debt integration and mill restructuring.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC sits at ~6.5%, oscillating between 1% in downcycles and 8-11% at temporary cyclical peaks. Operating margins historically average 3-7% and turned negative in 2024-2025 during packaging demand softness and mill closures. FCF conversion is volatile due to high maintenance capex (~$1B+/year). The January 2025 acquisition of DS Smith increased total debt to ~$9.7B, stretching leverage during an operating trough.
